A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RBC watermarking work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison across pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original watermark detection, robustness, and generation-quality experiments using Llama-3-8B and Llama-3-8B-Instruct.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons and paraphrasing-attack outcomes in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The correlated binary sampling channel, RBC generation and detection procedures, LDPC and one-to-one variants, and Algorithms 1–8 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 6.2 adds evaluation on text paraphrased using Llama-3-8B, introducing a distinct attack scenario. The story, news article, and book-report tasks, generation prompts, and base/instruction-model coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 3 and 5 add Huo et al. (2024)'s token-specific watermark and Hu et al. (2024)'s δ and γ reweighting methods. These substantially broaden the base-model comparisons beyond the existing Kirchenbauer distribution-shift baselines and RBC variants. The instruction-model comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a paraphrasing procedure using Llama-3-8B with the prompt 'Paraphrase the following text :' and specifies tail-bound-based p-values for the new Hu et al. comparisons. The retained generation design, swap/deletion rates, and detection thresholds are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new paraphrasing test in Section 6.2 and Table 2 extends the existing swap, deletion, and round-trip translation robustness analyses. The code comparison, instruction-model analysis, perplexity evaluation, and Appendix F case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 responses per prompt at each generation length and retain the same standard-error reporting practices. No changes to seeds, repeated-run counts, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 3 and 5 substantially revise base-model results and add comparator and paraphrasing outcomes. At the retained 150-token setting, Table 1 changes LDPC/one-to-one detection from 95%/97% to 88.1%/85.5%, reversing their ordering. Short-text table entries now summarize 30 rather than 20 tokens and therefore are not same-length performance comparisons. Appendix C.2 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, entropy bounds, Theorems 5.3–5.4, and Appendix D proofs are unchanged. The added reference to Hu et al.'s tail bounds supplies a baseline evaluation procedure without introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about distortion-free RBC watermarking, robustness, competitive detection power, simplicity, and applicability across language models.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 qualifies the detectability advantage as applying when token counts are small and removes the claim of requiring approximately half as many tokens. The entropy and generation-quality interpretations and Section 7.1 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents the token-specific baseline's default checkpoint, its predicted δ and γ parameters, the reweighting baselines' p-value calculation, and the paraphrasing prompt. RBC hyperparameters, Appendix B compute information, and Appendix E generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Hu et al. unbiased-watermark and Huo et al. token-specific-watermark papers, with brief descriptions in Section 6.1. The broader research positioning and Appendix A related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the experimental prose, with corrected robustness cross-references and an erroneous 'base' model mention changed to 'Instruct', consistent with the existing experiment. Yan Sun is added to the author list. The section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain rows and an attack group and are condensed onto one page. Table 1 clarifies that Mean P is the exponential of mean log p-value. Figures 3 and 5 receive additional curves, legends, and revised scales; Figure 4 moves without content changes. Other displays are preserved.

improvement.justification: Comparisons with unbiased alternatives and the direct paraphrasing test address gaps in v1's empirical support, while Section 6.1 gives a more qualified interpretation. The gain is limited by a new reporting inconsistency: v2 Table 1 gives the 150-token δ=1 baseline a median p-value of 7.0e-4 but 72.4% detection at a 1e-4 threshold, while Figure 3 plots detection below 40%. This weakens confidence in that specific comparison.
